Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
header:
Date: 2027-09-12
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Pareto CTO), Maya Patel (Pareto Lead ML Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Pareto PM)
Recording: yes
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE at Redwood. Priya from our solutions team is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: Good, thanks. We've been excited to dig into model selection, so appreciate the time.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Great, quick agenda — understand your workloads, context length needs, multilingual requirements, and then walk through Hosted/Dedicated/Private tradeoffs plus model options for open models.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Sounds perfect. I'll give a quick overview of what we're trying to build.
[00:26] Carlos Ruiz: Yep, and I'll jump in on product constraints and timelines.
[00:29] Jordan Lee: So Pareto Tech is building an insights assistant for enterprise documents, emails, and multi-source data connectors. Primary needs: long-form summarization (we're targeting up to 25k-32k token docs), multilingual support (English, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese), and the ability to call out to tools — like our internal DB connectors and a retrieval system.
[00:50] Alex Chen: Great, that helps. When you say tool-calling, is that function-calling-style external calls, or more of a retrieval hook?
[00:58] Maya Patel: Both. We want the model to optionally call our vector store retriever, and in some flows call out to a structured tool that can run SQL-ish queries against customer datasets.
[01:08] Priya Singh: Understood. A couple clarifying Qs: 1) Is latency critical? 2) Expected QPS? 3) Any regulatory constraints about hosting?
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Latency target for interactive flows is around 700-900 ms 95th, but for batch summarization overnight that's not critical. QPS will be modest initially — maybe 5-10 RPS at peak for the pilot. Regulatory: customers are mostly in US/EMEA; some healthcare partners so data residency and audit logs are required.
[01:36] Alex Chen: Thanks. That actually maps well to our three deployment modes. For initial pilot Hosted is often fastest to get started, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) handles strict residency and audit requirements.
[01:50] Carlos Ruiz: If we start Hosted, how hard is migrating to Dedicated or Private later?
[01:55] Priya Singh: It's designed to be smooth — same API and rollout configs. For Private you'll need network setup (VPC peering or on-prem appliance), and we do a short integration to wire up KMS and audit.
[02:07] Maya Patel: On model selection: we're evaluating open models to keep costs down and avoid vendor lock. Which open models do you recommend for 32k context and multilingual quality?
[02:18] Alex Chen: For long context, we often recommend Falcon-180B-instruct variants for solid long-context performance, Mistral's latest long-context families, and Llama-3-like families (where licensed). But note that some of the 'long' context patches have different memory/latency profiles.
[02:36] Priya Singh: Also worth flagging Redwood-verified performance profiles — we benchmarked several open families on throughput and latency across our runtime. For example, Falcon variants give good per-token speed on certain GPU configs, while quantized Llama-3 variants give cost savings if you can accept slightly higher latency.
[02:53] Jordan Lee: Any caveats around tool-calling and instruction-following? We need consistent function/tool calling for structured outputs.
[03:02] Priya Singh: Function calling works across model families, but robustness varies. Some Mistral/Falcon instruction-tuned variants handle structured tool-calls reliably. For highest fidelity we recommend running a prompt-eval suite (we can provide) and look at hit rates for function-calls.
[03:16] Maya Patel: Regarding multilingual, are these models natively good at Japanese and Portuguese, or do we need fine-tuning?
[03:24] Alex Chen: Many open models have weaker coverage in some non-Latin languages. Mistral and some Llama-3 variants tend to be better out of the box for European languages; Japanese often benefits from additional fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation. For Portuguese and Spanish most instruction-tuned models do OK.
[03:40] Carlos Ruiz: Do you support on-the-fly retrieval augmentation + tool-calling within the same request?
[03:45] Priya Singh: Yes — our runtime supports retrieval-augmented generation with KV cache management. You can route to retrievers and then call tools; we have examples in the SDK. There are caveats around payload size and effective context management for 32k docs.
[03:58] Jordan Lee: On cost, what should we expect per 1k tokens for hosted vs dedicated? Ballpark is fine.
[04:05] Alex Chen: Ballpark, hosted with open models on our shared infra might be X cents per 1k tokens (we'll send exact pricing), Dedicated is lower per-token at scale but requires a committed monthly spend. Private has higher setup and infra costs but can be most economical if you're running large steady volume. We'll follow up with a TCO calc for your expected pilot volumes.
[04:25] Maya Patel: We need to test memory usage for 32k sequences. Do you expose kernel/compilation knobs?
[04:31] Priya Singh: Our runtime selects kernels based on sequence length and hardware. For extremely long contexts we use specialized attention kernels and continuous batching. We can also recommend quantization profiles — 4-bit quant can reduce memory significantly but may affect quality.
[04:45] Jordan Lee: Any recommended GPU types for Dedicated? A100, H100?
[04:49] Priya Singh: For 32k and large models, H100 gives best latency/throughput but is pricier. A100 is widely used and good for most long-context workloads depending on batch sizing. We can provide model-specific perf numbers.
[04:59] Alex Chen: Priya, can you walk through a sample pilot plan?
[05:02] Priya Singh: Sure. Phase 1 (1-2 weeks): sample prompt set + ground truth, Redwood sends evaluation harness and we run models (Hosted). Phase 2 (2-4 weeks): joint benching with your retrieval/tooling, maybe spin up Dedicated trial for perf. Phase 3: Pilot (4-8 weeks) — can be hosted or dedicated; if regulatory needs arise move to Private. We'll collect latency/cost/quality metrics.
[05:25] Maya Patel: For the eval, can you include function-calling success rates and hallucination checks?
[05:30] Priya Singh: Yes, we have eval templates that measure function-calling accuracy, hallucination rate, multilingual BLEU-like metrics for structured tasks.
[05:39] Jordan Lee: You mentioned KV cache and prefix caching — can those help with repeated summarization of overlapping docs?
[05:46] Priya Singh: Absolutely. Prefix and KV caching reduce repeated compute for similar prefixes. It helps a lot when users re-query similar documents.
[05:52] Carlos Ruiz: On security — we need SSO/SAML, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. How do these map across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
[06:03] Alex Chen: Hosted includes SSO & RBAC and audit logs; for enterprise we offer customer-managed KMS integration. Dedicated adds network isolation and stricter commit-based SLAs. Private gives you the most control — you manage KMS, networking, and we can run an on-prem control plane if needed.
[06:19] Maya Patel: Does Redwood ship agent or connectors for our retriever? We use an in-house vector store with custom metadata.
[06:25] Priya Singh: We have SDK examples and a connector pattern. For custom vector stores we usually do a lightweight adapter; it rarely needs heavy engineering.
[06:33] Jordan Lee: Anything else we should be thinking about for migration and rollouts?
[06:37] Alex Chen: Rollouts can be canary or A/B. You can pin model versions and fallback to smaller variants in overload. Also, quality regression alerts tie to prompt sets so you can detect when a new model or quantization causes regressions.
[06:51] Carlos Ruiz: Timeline-wise, we'd like a pilot starting in October. Is that feasible?
[06:55] Alex Chen: Yes — if you can ship the sample prompt set and access to retriever endpoints we can get evaluations running within two weeks.
[07:03] Maya Patel: For the evals, what's the recommended sample size? We have a corpus of ~10k docs but can sample 200-500 representative ones.
[07:12] Priya Singh: 200-500 prompt/doc pairs is ideal for early model selection. Include edge cases and multilingual examples.
[07:20] Jordan Lee: OK that works. Any red flags on the model side for 32k sequences?
[07:24] Priya Singh: Main things: memory footprint and latency spikes. Also tool-calling token budgets if you pre-pend long retrieval context; you may need to chunk or summarize retrieved chunks before feeding.
[07:36] Alex Chen: We'll attach our guidance doc on best practices for long context and retrieval.
[07:41] Carlos Ruiz: Competitors — we did a bake-off with Anthropic earlier; they were good on instruction-following but cost was high. Curious how Redwood's open model approach compares.
[07:50] Alex Chen: Anthropic is strong on guardrails and safety, but with open models you get cost flexibility. Redwood focuses on giving you control — we can help tune quantization, batching, and model selection to match cost/quality.
[08:02] Maya Patel: Who will own the integration during pilot? On our side Maya and an infra engineer. On Redwood side?
[08:09] Alex Chen: Alex AE leads the program, Priya as SE will lead technical integration and benchmarking.
[08:15] Jordan Lee: Great. To recap, can you list deliverables?
[08:19] Alex Chen: Sure — pricing/TCO by 9/14, private deploy/SOC2 docs by 9/16, evaluation harness and sample prompts template today, and we'll schedule a follow-up technical deep-dive with Priya next week.
[08:33] Carlos Ruiz: That lines up. Any open questions from Redwood?
[08:36] Priya Singh: Just one: do you have any hard constraints on tokenization or proprietary tokenization needs?
[08:42] Maya Patel: No, standard UTF-8 workflows. We do have some domain-specific tokens but can handle via tokenizer customization if needed.
[08:51] Jordan Lee: Final thing — who will be the legal/sourcing contact for Private if we go that route? I'll loop in Sourcing but for now Carlos will be point.
[08:58] Carlos Ruiz: Yep I'll be the point.
[09:01] Alex Chen: Excellent. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pricing and docs.
[09:06] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:09] [call ends]
